assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 supplementary character monograph series/gakuen-idolmaster/07_DEFINITIVE_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPHS/GKM_JUO_KUNIO.md (18,889 bytes; status canonical, empty supersession arrays, veto false), a self-contained portrait of Juo Kunio across the admitted tutorial, selected Dear routes, song and card communications, support and event stories, Produce branches and the Unit Story at Source Lock 1.2 revision 88, plus the separately evidenced school-song lyric credit and spoken-role credit. assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Kunio's appearances within the admitted stories at Source Lock 1.2 revision 88, from the tutorial welcome to the winter awards and the Unit Story H.I.F. result. Within D-CHINA the order is the summer Prima Stella deadline, then the H.I.F. request with no penalty, then the refused judge's seat; N.I.A. is located in Sena's Dear 012. assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The opening section gives an organizing principle: confidence in what he sees in people, trust expressed by handing them something very difficult, and authority used so that the resulting work and risk fall on them (K1, K3-K8). It predicts overreach as well as generosity: relaying the Kuramoto grandfather's summer Prima Stella demand after questioning haste (K6-K7), the unhelpful raw-talent comparison between China and Sena (K6), and drafting the student Producer as the fourth person to take N.I.A. criticism (K10). Not B: the portrait states it supports no comprehensive account of his inner life, and it does not settle which of family pride, a grudge against Kuroi or a developmental criterion decides when they pull apart on an evaluation; no route shows whether he was the deciding vote at the H.I.F. unit result or held its criterion before deliberation (K14), and the motive order in the N.I.A. decision is left open (K10). Being unable to tell which motive decides an evaluation is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. Not D: the principle carries discriminating conditions (a defined job needing reliable completion versus an unlikely student's promise; a favor of resources versus a favor of decision power) that support narrow prediction.

The portrait affirmatively says the sources show an accumulation of tests of a working disposition and do not securely depict a personality change from the tutorial welcome through the late awards (Limits section). Situations are ordered inside one route (D-CHINA: the summer deadline, the H.I.F. request with no penalty and the fifty-gram message, then the refused judge's seat, K6, K8), but the winter Dear ceremonies and the Produce failure branch are divergent outcomes, not ordered states (K13). Not C: no located change of state or ordered progression of his own condition. Not E: the scenes are distributed across many stories and each keeps its own outcome.

'His speech in the room' gives an individuated, listener-conditioned written register: わし; おぬし for a familiar addressee below or across his authority; じゃ and related forms; emphatic せい / みせい; surname-and-given-name plus 君 in formal acknowledgment; bare 星南 in direct counsel; 若きプロデューサー候補生 or プロデューサー to confer a role; 倉本爺 for his old friend; 黒井の小僧 for Kuroi; ceremonial 我々 as a representative; the laugh that opens the tutorial, the broken-off name question, pleasantry as a short preface to an imperative, and the dry fifty-gram joke (K1, K4, K6, K8, K10, K12-K14). The portrait warns against reducing him to a constant roar. Not A: few quoted lines and no line inventory; the stock elderly register is individuated mainly by address forms and rhetorical moves; delivery, timbre and singing are explicitly open (voiced takes, text labels and perspective can come apart; only the lyric and spoken-role credits are established, K14-K16). Not C: address and rhetorical shifts are located per addressee and occasion closely enough to constrain illustrative written Japanese.

Ordinary conduct is one low-stakes episode: startled by Hiro's Halloween prank, he summons her Producer and sends a cake with a promise to be harder to surprise next time (K4-K5). The portrait states the cake is no finding about his tastes and that his assets, health, home routine, diet and private hobbies are unknown (Limits section). Not D: no distributed ordinary conduct outside institutional work.

The portrait rests its qualification on differentiated conduct toward a new student (laugh, challenge, role conferred, K1), an unorthodox candidate (backing Hiro's admission despite a zero practical score and naming her capacity to surprise, K3-K4), a peer sponsor (the Kuramoto grandfather: provocation over whose granddaughter is cuter, a favor turned into an order with a deadline, then the judge's seat refused, K6, K8), his granddaughter (pride; questioning haste yet relaying pressure; subordinate producing authority with stated limits, K6-K7, K9), an adult rival (seizing a public opening against Kuroi and enjoying the imagined reaction, K10) and a public audience (formal, affirmative announcement of whoever won, K13-K14). It states how the response changes with the relationship and with what is asked (resources versus decision; a defined professional job versus a promising start). Not A: most ties rest on one or two scenes; the son tie is reported (Ryuusei as referent is strongly supported, not stated), and private family conduct with Sena is thin. Not C: the conditioning is explicit and located across six relationship types.

There is no inner voice. Interior evidence is self-report at a few points: Sena as his pride and how dear she is (K6), his stated resentment at being left out of planning N.I.A. (K10), and the promise to be harder to surprise (K5). The portrait says it supports no comprehensive account of his inner life. Not D: interior access is not distributed; only outward speech is available.

Located modes with triggers: provocation and its cost (praising Sena to his old friend, after which others carry the competitive outcome, K6); bounded refusal of a peer (refusing the judge's seat and talking the grandfather out of it, with a voiced suspicion that the Producer encouraged the request, K8); institutional rivalry (pre-emptive announcement of Sena's N.I.A. entry before Kuroi can evade it, shared public exposure, and an explicit boundary keeping the newcomer contest intact, K10). Not B: one or two scenes per mode; his actual exchange with Kuroi is unseen (the inserted Kuroi line is imagined, K10), and open confrontation with his son or granddaughter is unshown. Not D: each mode carries its trigger and boundary.

Located competition-integrity positions with stated reasons: family-funded songs are legitimate resources an idol deploys, while a family member's official power over the verdict is refused (K8); the H.I.F. contains no flukes or miracles (K8); N.I.A. must remain a contest for new idols even after he urges the announcement (K10); the unit result is voiced with the dissent and the criterion of who made others shine (K14). The resource-versus-verdict line supports narrow extrapolation. Not B: no staged weighing or interior deliberation is shown, and the portrait says his judgments cannot be called reliably fair because he can articulate a defensible result; the deadline relayed from one grandfather to two students shows him passing on pressure he questioned (K6-K7). Not D: the boundaries are located with reasons in more than one route.

Instances with stated function: the laugh that opens the tutorial (K1); the fifty-gram joke naming the gap between formal removal of a penalty and pressure the recipient still feels (K8); laughing at the picture of Kuroi's fury (K10); provoking his friend with praise of Sena (K6); receiving Hiro's prank and prolonging it with a cake and a promise (K4-K5). The portrait distinguishes low-stakes playful recovery from high-stakes institutional response and says the private-wit evidence does not extend to all intimacy. Not B: a handful of instances. Not D: function and stake-conditioning are stated.

One compact, independently reviewed portrait (18,889 bytes) routes its claims to locators K1-K16 and names its absences (prior biography, private life, performed voice). The evidence matrix behind those locators and the project's underlying readings are not curated on this subject. Not B: a single derived item without ledgers on the row. Not D: its routes cover the declared boundary.

Affirmative bounds stated by the portrait: the divergent winter ceremonies, where he names Hiro, China, Saki or Kotone and identifies Sena or Ume as incumbent, show his pride in Sena cannot explain every decision he announces (K13); he refused the grandfather's judge's seat (K8); Sena's authority to produce is subordinate, with stated limits (K9); he gives no technical refutation of the Producer's assessment of Hiro (K3); he does not author the cover-live song choice (K12); the imagined Kuroi line is not Kuroi's actual reaction (K10); voiced takes do not establish delivery (K14-K16). Not B: mostly bounding statements, with no disconfirmed forecasts or corrected earlier states. Not D: several bounds are located against specific overreadings.

Each story keeps its own outcome: the tutorial, Hiro's recalled interview and Dear 001, the D-CHINA sequence in order, Sena's Dear 012 for N.I.A., the divergent winter Dear outcomes and a Produce failure branch, and the Unit Story's H.I.F. result (K1-K14). Not B: no calendar placing his scenes on one timeline, and alternate outcomes stand in for states. Not D: outcomes and route sequences are kept apart and located.

conditions: Output is illustrative written Japanese, never quotation; no timbre, melody of speech, singing or performed delivery is claimed (K14-K16).

Register: わし, じゃ forms, emphatic せい / みせい; おぬし for a familiar addressee below or across his authority; surname-and-given-name plus 君 in formal acknowledgment; bare 星南 in counsel; 若きプロデューサー候補生 or プロデューサー to confer a role; 倉本爺 and 黒井の小僧 as sampled; ceremonial 我々 as representative.
Rhetorical moves: a laugh or pleasantry before an imperative, interruption into acknowledgment, praise attached to a difficult request, dry understatement (the fifty-gram joke); not a constant roar.

Interlocutors are the sampled ones: a student Producer, an idol candidate, Sena, the Kuramoto grandfather, Kuroi by reference, a ceremony audience. Another teacher or a comparable adult peer is a separate, lower-confidence condition limited to the register rules.
No private family, intimate or domestic dialogue; the son tie is reported, not staged.
scenario_readiness.note: The address forms and rhetorical moves constrain illustrative written Japanese for him as headmaster with the sampled addressees closely enough for bounded use. Performed delivery and private or intimate speech are not constrained.

conditions: A surprising candidate with poor measured skill: predict that he may name a reason people will keep watching and authorize a promising start, without a lesson plan or attention to physical limits (K3-K4); for a defined paid or professional job, predict criteria of ability and reliability (K12).

An established figure or old friend asks a favor: predict routing it through a trusted Producer or student with familiarity and an expectation of results, possibly with a deadline (K6-K7); permit resources the idol deploys, refuse a family member's official power over the verdict (K8).

Another institution outmaneuvers him: predict remembering the slight, seizing a public opening, enjoying the likely reaction, sharing exposure with those he involves, and setting an explicit boundary on the new opportunity (K10).
A family member loses a public contest: predict a formal, affirmative announcement of the winner (K13); private consolation and lobbying are unknown.
A familiar person catches him off guard at low stakes: playful recovery is plausible (K4-K5); it does not transfer to high-stakes institutional responses.
Include his mistakes: passing on pressure he questioned, attaching belief to a very hard assignment that others carry, drafting students into adults' quarrels, and curiosity standing in for teaching.
Exclude any prediction of which result he would choose when his own vote decides between Sena or a favored student and a stronger field; the evidence does not establish his criterion or vote (K14).

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Hatsuboshi at Source Lock 1.2 revision 88 within the admitted stories, from the tutorial welcome to the winter awards and the Unit Story H.I.F. result. No secure change of disposition is shown across them, so one disposition applies throughout; a named route outcome (a Dear winter result or a Produce failure branch) is an alternate outcome, not a later state. His industry past is known only as his son's inheritance of 100 Pro from him.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: A student Producer or idol candidate he admits, entrusts or challenges; his granddaughter Sena as pride and as subordinate producer; the Kuramoto grandfather as old friend and quarrelsome peer sponsor; Kuroi as institutional rival; a ceremony audience. His son appears only by report; another teacher or agency executive is a separate, lower-confidence transfer; romantic partners are unsampled.
setting_constraints: Hatsuboshi Academy and its competitions and events as the game presents them at Source Lock 1.2 revision 88: admission, the Producer Course, H.I.F., N.I.A., awards and professional recommendations.

No pre-game agency career, no home or private life, no health, finance or romance premise, no event beyond the admitted stories, no cross-series setting, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Novel institutional scenes can be predicted from the five-row conditional profile and the resource-versus-verdict boundary. Evaluations where his own criterion decides between family pride and the field, his prior career and private life are excluded.
One low-stakes episode (the Halloween prank and the cake, K4-K5); the portrait states his home routine, diet, health and private hobbies are unknown and the cake is no finding about his tastes.

conditions: Only questions about favors and influence in a contest he oversees: resources an idol deploys are permitted, a family member's power over the verdict is refused (K8).
Only questions about the purpose of a contest he backs: the newcomer competition stays a newcomer competition even when he brings in established stars (K10).
Not his own evaluative criterion or vote, which no route establishes (K14), and not dilemmas outside institutional competition.
Predict that pressure he questions may still be passed on (K6-K7); an articulated defensible result is not evidence he is reliably fair.
scenario_readiness.note: Narrow competition-integrity questions of the kind sampled can be predicted from located positions with reasons. General moral reasoning and his weighing of fairness against family pride are not supported.
The portrait states the materials give no basis for reconstructing his romantic and intimate life and that his past marriage is unknown.

conditions: As Hatsuboshi's headmaster at Source Lock 1.2 revision 88: welcoming and challenging students, backing an exception, delegating a favor to a trusted Producer or student, entering or bounding a competition, announcing results, recommending students for outside work (K1-K14).
The class teacher supplies practical orientation; predict mission and challenge from him, not teaching (K1).
Exclude his pre-game 100 Pro career, the shared mechanics of admission decisions, the actual ownership and governance of N.I.A. (K10-K11), and his vote or criterion in evaluation deliberations (K14).
scenario_readiness.note: His headmaster functions are the best-sampled domain: welcome and role conferral, exceptional admission, delegation of favors, competition entry and boundaries, ceremony and professional recommendation.

known_limits.statement: All claims rest on one 18,889-byte derived portrait; most relationship and conflict modes rest on one or two scenes, and no held-out test of its conditional profile is reported.
The portrait states it supports no comprehensive account of his inner life; interior evidence is limited to a few self-reports (Sena as his pride, resentment at the N.I.A. omission).

The sources show repeated tests of one working disposition and do not securely depict a personality change; winter Dear results and the Produce failure branch are alternate outcomes, not ordered states.

No route establishes whether he was the deciding vote at the H.I.F. unit result or held its criterion of who made others shine before deliberation, and the portrait says an articulated defensible result does not make him reliably fair; his own evaluative choices between family pride and a stronger field cannot be predicted.
Whether he saw the newcomers' interests in N.I.A. before the opportunity to embarrass Kuroi is left open; grudge, office and educational purpose are all read as operating in the same decision.
His announcements across divergent ceremonies preserve a public function and do not make him the unilateral chooser of results.

Voiced takes, text labels, projection cues and perspective can come apart; his delivery, timbre, singing and motion are not established. Only the school-song lyric credit and the spoken-role credit are evidenced.
The son tie and Ryuusei as the referent of 'my son' are reported or strongly supported rather than staged, and Kuroi's reaction to the N.I.A. announcement is imagined, not shown.
Prior biography and agency career, assets, health, home routine, diet, past marriage, romance, private hobbies and how he handles his own long-term loss are outside the evidence.
The evidence matrix behind locators K1-K16, the project's source-facing readings and its qualification record are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them.
